problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{4}xyz\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type II Regions

Given that $R$ is the type II region shown above, 
${∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V=$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a type II region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type II region enclosed between the back surface $x={u}_{1}(y,z)=1$ and the front surface $x={u}_{2}(y,z)=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/339d4658909da42d55a836af93c7fda425bbe8d0ce17f246b73a4ca28cb9f380.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,1\le x\le 3}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $yz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9\,⟺\,z=\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/879425adc3b1e78a7ea6a59740c9d8634ac13f62dea8eedc764bb5f1b07c92c2.png)

Hence, $D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}[{\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}2y[x]_{x=1}^{x=3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}4y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
